items.reason: The precondition 'the functional host's catalog database holds the demo catalog: 13 brands, 101 items' does not say how that is guaranteed. The existing CatalogApiTests share one database per test class through IClassFixture<CatalogApiFixture> and change it: UpdateCatalogItemWorksWithPriceUpdate reprices item 1 (Daybird) to 1.99, DeleteCatalogItem deletes items 5 (B&R) and 6 (Raptor Elite), and AddCatalogItem adds an item to brand 13 (XE). A test written in that class would see Daybird 49.99 become 1.99, B&R 10 become 9 and XE 3 become 4 or 5, depending on order. The case must state that it runs in its own test class with its own catalog database, which no changing test shares, so the exact values hold. TC-01 and TC-03 should state the same precondition.

AC1 says the Brands link is 'next to' Shop all. TC-04 and TC-05 require it to be 'the navigation link immediately after Shop all', which is stricter than the story. They should accept the link directly before or after Shop all.

items.reason: Precondition: own test class with its own CatalogApiFixture instance, and no test that changes catalog data shares that database. BrandSummaryTests uses [Collection(CatalogApiCollection.Name)] (ICollectionFixture<CatalogApiFixture>) shared with CatalogApiTests, which reprices item 1, deletes items 5/6 and adds an XE item and relies on undo code to put them back. The exact order and brand set depend on that undo succeeding. Use IClassFixture<CatalogApiFixture> on BrandSummaryTests and revert the CatalogApiTests/CatalogApiCollection changes.

Same shared-fixture deviation: the exact per-brand counts and lowest prices (Daybird 49.99, B&R 10, Raptor Elite 11, XE 3) hold only if CatalogApiTests' undo PUT/POST/DELETE calls all succeed, because the case runs on the database CatalogApiTests changes. The precondition requires an unshared database.

Same shared-fixture deviation: the sum of 101 and the 14-entry count are asserted on a database that CatalogApiTests changes and is expected to restore. The precondition requires its own CatalogApiFixture instance.
